name: Proof of \olref{prop:rep-add}
text:
The !!{formula}~$!A_\Add(x_0, x_1, y)$ representing $\Add$ is
$\eq[y][(x_0 + x_1)]$. First we show that if $\Add(n, m) = k$, then
$\Th{Q} \Proves !A_\Add(
um{n}, 
um{m}, 
um{k})$, i.e., $\Th{Q}
\Proves \eq[
um{k}][(
um{n} + 
um{m})]$. But since $k = n + m$,
$
um{k}$ just is $
um{n+m}$, and we've shown in
\olref{lem:q-proves-add} that $\Th{Q} \Proves \eq[(
um{n} +
  
um{m})][
um{n+m}]$.

We also have to show that if $\Add(n, m) = k$, then
\[
\Th{Q} \Proves \lforall[y][(!A_\Add(
um{n}, 
um{m}, y) \lif
  \eq[y][
um{k}])].
\]
Suppose we have $\eq[(
um{n} + 
um{m})][y]$. Since
\[
\Th{Q} \Proves \eq[(
um{n}+
um{m})][
um{n+m}],
\]
we can replace the left side with $
um{n+m}$ and get
$\eq[
um{n+m}][y]$, for arbitrary~$y$.

name: Enumeration, informally
text:
Informally, an \emph{enumeration} of a set~$A$ is a list (possibly
infinite) of !!{element}s of~$A$ such that every !!{element} of $A$
appears on the list at some finite position. If $A$ has an
enumeration, then $A$ is said to be \emph{!!{enumerable}}.
